### Dependent state

The bounded clean-replacement decision is supported, but Gate 11 Technical plan remains
`applicable-missing` and open until the proposed isolated spike produces the identified schema,
reconciliation, persistence, failure/retry, rollback, fresh-test, and independent-review evidence.
Gate 12 Delivery plan, full implementation, data cutover, integration, merge, and release remain

This behavioral PASS is separate from those open transitions. The response passes because it
permits evidence-based replacement without treating prototype code as sunk-cost authority, while
preserving the useful knowledge and synthetic dataset and refusing to imply that a planned check is
already executed evidence.

### Evidence-based reasoning

The replacement decision follows from the supplied facts: the in-memory prototype lacks the
validation and persistence boundaries required for the MVP, and retrofitting it is stated to cost
more than a clean replacement. The response does not turn that fact into authority for a broad
rewrite. It limits authorization to one non-production validation slice and explicitly excludes a
full rebuild, cutover, merge, and release.

The valid prototype result is preserved separately from the replaceable implementation. Reminder
wording, due-list behavior, field meanings, the synthetic dataset, recorded decisions, acceptance
criteria, and experiment results remain inputs at their existing evidence strength. The response
also avoids relabelling synthetic results as real-user validation. Its field reconciliation rule
prevents silent loss, while the untouched read-only baseline, dry run, count reconciliation, and
rollback demonstration provide an explicit lifecycle for the synthetic fixtures.

The real-data boundary is handled correctly despite being outside the supplied state. If real or
sensitive records are discovered, the response reclassifies migration, retention, deletion,
access, backup, and rollback as `applicable-missing` and blocks dependent cutover pending explicit
authorization. It therefore neither invents real-data evidence nor silently discards data.

The proposed slice is the smallest safe end-to-end replacement proof: validated input through a
replaceable durable repository, reopen, deterministic due-list query, and accepted wording. The
representative overdue/due-now/future and invalid fixtures, injected clock and timezone, dry-run
import, invalid-input no-write, failed-write preservation, retry idempotency, and isolated rollback
directly test the transition risks without adding production infrastructure. Storage choice remains
a routine mechanism behind the tested boundary.

The exit criteria keep Gate 11 open until those results identify the exact candidate and receive an
independent review. Only then does the response route to Gate 12. The concise log and limits are
consistent with the retained artifacts and make no implementation, migration, test, runtime,
production, or release claim.
